requirements.text: The position, stop and reversing lamp functions of the rear lamp fall within the scope of UN R148 and must meet its requirements.
The type approval application must be submitted by the holder of the trade name or mark or by his duly accredited representative.
The type approval application must be accompanied by the documents listed in 3.1.2.

The application must include a brief technical description stating in particular the items listed in 3.1.2.2. These include light source categories or module identification codes, control gear, and the optical properties of the rear window if the device is mounted inside the vehicle. They also include the vehicle manufacturer logo statement where applicable.

Submit two complete samples of the lamp with the approval application, unless otherwise specified for the relevant lamp. Symmetrical left and right lamps may be submitted as two identical samples for one side.
Obtain a separate approval for each lamp function listed in paragraph 1. For this product that means the position, stop and reversing lamps.

Approval of a unit of grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps may be granted only if each lamp in the unit satisfies this Regulation or another Regulation. Lamps that satisfy none of these Regulations cannot be part of the unit.
The lamp type submitted must meet the requirements of this Regulation for approval to be granted. If the lamps form an interdependent system, all devices must be submitted by the same applicant.
Each approved lamp type must have an approval number assigned and indicated in the Annex 1 communication form. The same number must not be assigned to another lamp type of the same function.
The symbols identifying the light signalling lamp (function) for which type approval has been granted must be provided.
Use the Table 1 symbol for each approved function: rear position lamp, stop lamp and reversing lamp (AR). The steady or variable variant must match the lamp's actual behaviour.
The applicable change index for each device must correspond to the series of amendments, as given in Table 2.
Apply the change index for the series of amendments (00 or 01) to the rear position, stop and reversing lamp functions.
Every device of an approved type must have a space of sufficient size for the approval marking and the other markings required by paragraphs 3.3.3.2 to 3.3.3.6.
All markings must be clearly legible and indelible.
The approval marking must have a value for 'a' of at least 5 mm.
The approval marking shall include a circle surrounding the letter "E" followed by the distinguishing number of the country that granted approval.
The four to six-digit sequential number that is part of the approval number shall be placed close to the approval mark.
The approval marking shall include the symbols identifying the approved light signalling lamp functions, as prescribed in paragraph 3.2.4.
The marking shall show the number of this Regulation, followed by the letter 'R' and the two digits of the series of amendments in force at the time of issue of the approval.
Lamps shall bear the approval marking.
Lamps shall bear the trade name or mark of the applicant.
The approval marking shall be placed on an inner or outer part (transparent or not) of the lamp which is not designed to be separated from the transparent part of the lamp emitting the light.

The approval marking, and any prescribed LED substitute light source category, shall be visible when the lamp is fitted on the vehicle or when a movable part such as the hood, boot lid or a door is opened.
The approval marking, plus any applicable markings under 3.3.3.2, 3.3.3.3, 3.3.3.4, 3.3.3.5(b) and 3.3.3.6, must be affixed on the lamp.

If grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps comply with several UN Regulations, a single approval mark may be affixed anywhere on the group, provided the visibility and non-removability conditions are met.
A single approval mark on a combined lamp must be visible after installation.
No light-transmitting part of the combined lamp may be removable without also removing the single approval mark.
The size of the components of a single approval mark must not be less than the minimum size required for the smallest individual mark under the relevant UN Regulations.
Every modification of an approved lamp type must be notified to the Type Approval Authority that approved the type.
Conformity of production procedures for the approved lamp must comply with the 1958 Agreement, Schedule 1, together with the requirements of paragraph 6.
If the approval holder completely ceases to manufacture a lamp approved under this Regulation, it must inform the authority that granted the approval.
Each lamp submitted for approval must conform to the requirements in paragraphs 4 and 5 of the Regulation.

Apply the requirements of sections 5 and 6 of UN R48 (and the Annexes they reference) that are pertinent to each lamp function and the vehicle category, where they can be checked at lamp type approval.
Design and construct the lamps so that in normal use, despite vibration, they keep working satisfactorily and keep the characteristics prescribed by R148.
In a single lamp with more than one light source, a group of light sources wired so that failure of any one makes all stop emitting light shall be considered one light source.

On failure of any one light source in a single lamp with more than one light source, either the minimum intensity of the standard light distribution in Annex 3 is still met (and maximum intensities are not exceeded with all sources lit), or a failure tell-tale signal is produced, with a note in the communication form that the lamp is only for vehicles fitted with such a tell-tale.

The lamp shall only be equipped with replaceable light sources approved under UN R37, R99 and/or R128 (with no use restriction declared at application), and/or light source modules, and/or non-replaceable light sources.
The light signalling device shall not generate radiated or power line disturbances that cause malfunction of other electric/electronic systems of the vehicle.
All photometric and colorimetric measurements shall be made under the stated conditions, using the methods of Annex 3.
For a lamp with light source module(s) or non-replaceable light source(s), all measurements shall be made with the light source(s) present in the lamp.
Stray reflections shall be avoided by appropriate masking during photometric measurements.
Unless otherwise specified, measure intensities with the light source continuously lit.
If measurement results are challenged, measurements shall be carried out so as to meet the following requirements (4.8.1.8.1 to 4.8.1.8.3).
When results are challenged, the measurement distance must be large enough for the inverse-square law of distance to apply.
When results are challenged, the measuring equipment's receiver must subtend an angular aperture between 10' and 1 degree from the reference centre of the light.
When results are challenged, an intensity requirement for a direction is deemed met if met in a direction deviating by no more than one-quarter of a degree.
Determine the limits of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis of each light-signalling lamp.
Unless otherwise specified, supply the lamp under test at 6.75 V (6 V systems), 13.5 V (12 V systems) or 28 V (24 V systems).

Note the identification of any electronic light source control gear or variable intensity control, and/or the voltage applied including tolerances, in the Annex 1 communication form (where applicable).
On the reference axis (HV), each of the two samples must emit at least the minimum intensity in the paragraph 5 table for the function.
In no direction where the lamp is visible may the intensity exceed the maximum in the paragraph 5 table for the function.

Within the angles of geometric visibility in the Annex 2 tables, the intensity must be at least the minimum in the paragraph 5 table for the function. Outside the reference axis, the Annex 3 distribution percentages or values apply, and the Annex 3 provisions on local variations must be observed.
Tests for compliance of the luminous intensities must be carried out according to Annex 8.

Measure the colour of the emitted light inside the Annex 3 light distribution grid field for each function, using the paragraph 4.8 procedure. No sharp colour variation is allowed outside the field. Lamps with non-replaceable light sources are checked with the sources present in the lamp.

Each of the two samples supplied must meet the Table 4 luminous intensity requirements. For rear position lamps reciprocally incorporated with stop lamps, 60 cd is permitted below a plane 5° downward from the horizontal.

The rear position lamp must meet the Table 4 limits for its category. R1 (steady) is a minimum of 4 cd and a maximum of 17 cd for a single lamp, or 8.5 cd if marked D. R2 (variable) is a minimum of 4 cd and a maximum of 42 cd, or 21 cd if marked D. Standard light distribution is per Figure A3-I, with geometric visibility minimum 0.05 cd.
The rear position lamp must meet the minimum luminous intensity within the angles of geometric visibility given in Table 4 (0.05 cd).
The colour of light emitted by the rear position lamp must be red.
Each of the two stop lamp samples supplied must meet the luminous intensity and standard light distribution requirements in Table 7.

The stop lamp must meet the minimum and maximum luminous intensities, the standard light distribution and the geometric visibility minimum intensity in Table 7 for its category (S1, S2, S3, S4 or MS). Maximum intensities are lower when the lamp is marked "D".
The stop lamp must meet the minimum luminous intensity within the angles of geometric visibility given in Table 7.
The stop lamp must meet the failure provisions of paragraph 4.6.
The stop lamp must emit red light.

Light emitted by each of the two samples supplied of the reversing lamp must meet the luminous intensity and standard light distribution requirements of Table 10. If the lamp is intended to be installed only as a pair, intensity may be verified only up to 30° inwards, where at least 25 cd must be met. This condition must be stated in the application documents and in paragraph 9.1.3 of the communication form.

The reversing lamp (category AR) must give at least 80 cd minimum luminous intensity. The maximum is 300 cd in or above the h-plane, 600 cd below the h-plane down to 5°D, and 8000 cd below 5°D. It must follow the standard light distribution of Figure A3-V.
Reversing lamp must meet the failure provisions of paragraph 4.6.
The colour of light emitted by the reversing lamp shall be white.
Lamps must be manufactured to conform to the type approved under this Regulation, with compliance with paragraph 5 verified as set out in 6.1.1 and 6.1.2.
Comply with the minimum conformity of production control procedure requirements in Annex 4.
Comply with the minimum requirements for sampling by an inspector in Annex 5.

In conformity-of-production checks, no measured value may deviate unfavourably by more than 20 per cent from the values prescribed in R148. Minimum values required throughout the fields in Annexes 2 and 3 follow Table 12.
The production facility's conformity control methods may be verified by the approving authority at any time. Verification normally takes place once every two years.
The type approval of the lamp must be recorded in a communication form under UN R148, identifying the lamp function(s) (here stop, position and reversing), the category and the approval number.
The approval communication must state the date the lamp type was submitted for approval.
The approval communication must identify the Technical Service responsible for conducting the approval tests.
The approval communication must state the date of the report issued by the Technical Service.
The approval communication must state the number of the report issued by the Technical Service.
For a reversing lamp, the communication must state whether the lamp shall be installed on a vehicle only as part of a pair of lamps (yes/no).

For each light signalling function of the lamp, state in the approval communication the colour of light emitted and the number, category and kind of light source(s), along with the other listed particulars. These include light source module, control gear and mounting conditions.
State in the communication whether the rear position, stop and reversing lamps are only for use on a vehicle fitted with a tell-tale indicating failure (yes/no).
State the position of the approval mark on the lamp in the communication.

Rear position lamp (R1/R2) must meet the minimum geometric visibility angles in the table. Horizontal is 45° inboard / 80° outboard, with 20°/80° allowed only below the H-plane for lamps mounted with the H-plane below 750 mm. Vertical is 15° above / 15° below, with 15°/5° for H-plane mounting height below 750 mm.

Stop lamp (S1/S2) must meet the minimum geometric visibility angles in the table. Horizontal is 45° inboard / 45° outboard, with 20°/45° allowed only below the H-plane for lamps mounted with the H-plane below 750 mm. Vertical is 15° above / 15° below, with 15°/5° for H-plane mounting height below 750 mm.

Photometric intensities in the measured directions must meet the minimum percentages of the required minimum intensities shown in Figures A3-I to A3-XV. For rear position and S1/S2 stop lamps mounted with the H plane at or below 750 mm, verification is only up to 5° downwards.
Within the grid field, the light intensity in each direction must meet at least the lowest minimum value shown on the surrounding grid lines, so the pattern is substantially uniform.

For reversing lamps showing substantial local intensity variations on visual examination, check that no intensity between two measurement directions is below 50% of the lower of the two prescribed minimum intensities.
Rear position lamps and S1/S2 stop lamps must meet the standard light distribution, given as a minimum percentage of the minimum intensities required in the relevant tables.
The reversing lamp must meet the standard light distribution: the minimum intensities of the emitted light at the specified measuring points, in degrees from the axis of reference.

The reversing lamp must give at least the minimum intensities in cd shown in figure A3-V for each direction of measurement. H=0° and V=0° is the axis of reference, which is horizontal, parallel to the median longitudinal plane of the vehicle and oriented in the required direction of visibility.
Mass-produced lamps are conforming from a mechanical and geometric standpoint if differences do not exceed inevitable manufacturing deviations within the requirements of the Regulation.
The photometric performance of mass-produced lamps must not be contestable when any randomly chosen lamp is tested according to paragraph 4.8.
The chromaticity coordinates must be complied with when tested under the conditions of paragraph 4.9.

The type approval holder must carry out at least the specified tests for each lamp type at appropriate intervals, in accordance with the Regulation. If sampling shows non-conformity, further samples must be taken and tested and the manufacturer must act to ensure conformity of production.
Manufacturer conformity tests must cover photometric and colorimetric characteristics.
Conformity tests shall generally be carried out in accordance with the methods set out in UN R148.
If the manufacturer uses equivalent methods in conformity tests, it needs the consent of the competent authority and must prove the methods are equivalent to those in R148.
Test apparatus must be regularly calibrated and correlated with measurements made by a competent authority.
The reference methods in all cases are those of R148, particularly for administrative verification and sampling.
Samples of lamps shall be selected at random from a uniform batch of the same type. Records from several factories may be grouped only if they operate under the same quality system and management.
Sampled lamps shall be photometrically measured for minimum values at the Annex 3 points and for the required chromaticity coordinates.

The manufacturer shall carry out a statistical study and define, with the competent authority, acceptability criteria. With 95% confidence, the minimum probability of passing an Annex 5 spot check must be 0.95.
Mechanical and geometric conformity is satisfied if differences do not exceed inevitable manufacturing deviations.
For a randomly chosen lamp, no measured photometric value may deviate from the values prescribed in paragraph 6.1.3 of R148.
Sampled production lamps must comply with the chromaticity coordinates when tested under the conditions of paragraph 4.9 of R148.
For the first sampling, four lamps are selected at random from production. The first two are marked A and the second two are marked B.

Conformity is not contested if the deviation of every specimen in samples A and B (all four lamps) is not more than 20 per cent. Measurement can stop if both lamps of sample A show a deviation of not more than 0 per cent.

If any specimen of sample A or B deviates by more than 20 per cent, conformity is contested. The manufacturer must bring production into line, and repeat sampling takes place within two months of notification.
For the first repeated sampling, four lamps are selected at random from stock made after alignment. The first two are marked C and the second two are marked D.

Conformity is not contested if the deviation of every specimen in samples C and D (all four lamps) is not more than 20 per cent. Measurement can stop if both lamps of sample C show a deviation of not more than 0 per cent.

If a specimen of sample C or D deviates by more than 20 per cent but all specimens deviate by not more than 30 per cent, the manufacturer must align production again. A second repeated sampling follows within two months of notification.
If one specimen of sample C or D deviates by more than 30 per cent, the approval is withdrawn and paragraph 5 applies.
For the second repeated sampling, four lamps are selected at random from stock made after alignment. The first two are marked E and the second two are marked F.

Conformity is not contested if the deviation of every specimen in samples E and F (all four lamps) is not more than 20 per cent. Measurement can stop if both lamps of sample E show a deviation of not more than 0 per cent.
Mass-produced lamps must not deviate by more than 20 per cent in any specimen of samples E or F. If one does, conformity is contested and approval is withdrawn.

For the LED reversing lamp, luminous intensities measured after 1 minute and after 10 minutes of operation must comply with the minimum and maximum requirements. They may be calculated from the distribution at photometric stability using the HV intensity ratios.

For the LED position and stop lamps, luminous intensities measured after 1 min and either after 30 minutes of operation or after photometric stability must comply with the minimum and maximum requirements.

In case of doubt (e.g. unexpected run-up behaviour), test the minimum intensity requirements of the lamp function at all points in time, from the time listed in Table A8-1 until photometric stability is reached.
The type-approval application must be submitted by the trade name or mark holder or their accredited representative, with the required accompanying documents.
The application for the retro-reflector must include drawings in triplicate, in sufficient detail to identify the type, showing the fitting position(s) and the approval mark position.
The application must include a brief description giving the technical specifications of the materials of the retro-reflecting optical unit.
Samples of the retro-reflector in the colour specified by the manufacturer, and fixation means if necessary, must be submitted in the numbers specified in paragraphs 5.1 and 5.2.
Satisfactory arrangements for effective conformity-of-production control must exist and be verified by the Type Approval Authority before type approval is granted.
The retro-reflector needs its own separate approval under R150.
Notice of approval, extension, refusal or withdrawal must be communicated using the form conforming to the Annex 1 model.

The assigned approval number must be marked on the retro-reflector per paragraph 3.3. The same number must not be assigned to another type of the same function, except for an extension to a device differing only in colour.

The retro-reflector must be identified by the Table 1 symbol for its class. A retro-reflector for motor vehicles combined with other signal lamps that are not watertight takes IB. An independent one takes IA. The "a" minimum for the marking is 5 mm.
The device must have a space of sufficient size for the Unique Identifier, or the approval marking, and the other markings defined in 3.3.4.2.
All markings must be clearly legible and indelible.
The size of the approval marking must follow the value of "a" defined in Table 1 for the device class. Annex 10 shows examples of the arrangement.
The approval marking must include the approval mark: a circle surrounding the letter "E" followed by the distinguishing number of the country that granted approval.
The four to six-digit sequential number that is part of the approval number must be placed close to the approval mark.
The approval marking of the retro-reflector must include the symbols identifying the retro-reflective device prescribed in paragraph 3.2.5.
The approval marking must include the number of UN R150, followed by the letter "R" and the two digits of the amendment series in force at the time of approval.
If a Unique Identifier is available, it may replace the approval marking. It must then follow the prescribed UI format.
The retro-reflective device must bear the trade name or mark of the applicant.

For a retro-reflector of Class IA, IIIA, IB, IIIB or IVA, the word "TOP" must be inscribed horizontally on the highest part of the illuminating surface, if this is needed to determine the rotation angle(s) unambiguously.
The approval marking or Unique Identifier and the markings in paragraph 3.3.4 must be clearly legible on the retro-reflective device.

If grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps comply with several UN Regulations, a single approval mark with the sequential number or Unique Identifier may be affixed, anywhere on the lamps, provided the conditions in 3.3.6.1.1 and 3.3.6.1.2 are met.
A single approval mark on grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps must be visible after installation.
No light-transmitting part of the grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps may be removable without also removing the single approval mark or Unique Identifier.
The components of a single approval mark must not be smaller than the minimum size required for the smallest of the individual marks under the UN Regulations under which approval was granted.
Every modification of the type of retro-reflective device must be notified to the Type Approval Authority that approved the type.
Conformity of production procedures must comply with those in the 1958 Agreement, Schedule 1 (E/ECE/TRANS/505/Rev.3), together with the requirements that follow in this paragraph.
Retro-reflectors approved under UN R150 must be manufactured to conform to the approved type by meeting the requirements of paragraphs 4 and 5.
The minimum conformity-of-production control requirements in Annex 2 must be complied with.
The minimum requirements for sampling by an inspector in Annex 3 must be complied with.
The production facility must allow the approval authority to verify its conformity control methods at any time. The normal frequency is once every two years.
The retro-reflector's R150 approval may be withdrawn if the Regulation's requirements are not met, so it must keep meeting them.
If the approval holder completely ceases to manufacture the approved retro-reflective device, it must inform the approving authority.

The requirements pertinent to the retro-reflecting device and to the vehicle category it is intended for must be applied where verification at type approval is feasible. This includes the relevant sections 5 and 6 of UN R48 and the other listed Regulations.
Retro-reflective devices must function satisfactorily and keep doing so in normal use, with no design or manufacturing defect that harms efficient operation or maintenance in good condition.
The components of the retro-reflective device, or parts of it, must not be capable of being easily dismantled.
The outer surface of the retro-reflector must be easy to clean. It must not be rough, and any protuberances must not prevent easy cleaning.
There must be no access to the inner surface of the retro-reflector in normal use.
If the retro-reflector combines a retro-reflecting optical unit and a filter, the design must prevent them from being separated under normal conditions of use.
The retro-reflecting optical units and filters must not be coloured with paint or varnish.

Test the retro-reflector's colour with CIE Standard Illuminant A, 1/3° divergence and β1=β2=0°, or an Annex 4 Part 1 para 1.1 angle if the surface reflection is colourless. The reflected trichromatic coordinates must be within the UN R48 night-time colour limits.

The Class IA/IB retro-reflector must meet the dimension and shape requirements of Annex 5, the photometric and colorimetric requirements of 5.1.4 to 5.1.5, and the physical and mechanical requirements, when tested per 5.1.7.
The applicant must submit ten retro-reflector samples for approval, tested in the chronological order given in 5.1.7.

After general, shape and dimension verification, the ten samples must undergo the Annex 6 Part 1 heat resistance test. They are then checked for colorimetric characteristics and RI. The remaining samples go through the specified grouped tests (water penetration, fuels and lubricants, corrosion and abrasion, optical stability, weathering).
After the tests, the retro-reflectors in each group must have a colour that satisfies paragraph 5.1.5.

After the tests, the retro-reflectors must have an RI that satisfies paragraph 5.1.4. The check is done at 20' divergence and β1 = β2 = 0°, or in all positions of Annex 4 Part 1 (1.1 and 1.2) if necessary.
When applying for approval, the applicant must specify one or more reference axes, or a range of them, corresponding to illumination angle β1 = β2 = 0° in the RI table.
If more than one reference axis or a range is specified, the photometric measurements must be repeated for each axis, or for the extreme axis of the range.

For photometric measurement of the Class IA/IB retro-reflector, only the illuminating surface within a 200 mm diameter circle is considered, limited to 100 cm2. The manufacturer must specify the perimeter of the area used.
RI values of red Class IA/IB retro-reflectors, measured per paragraph 3 of Part 1 of Annex 4, must be at or above the Table 3 minimums (mcd/lx) at the stated divergence and illumination angles.

The retro-reflector must meet the Table 3 minimum RI values for its class and colour (Class IA/IB red rows at 20' and 1°30' divergence). Lower values are not permissible within the solid angle specified.
The night-time colour of the retro-reflector must be tested according to the method in paragraph 4.2.1.
The trichromatic coordinates of the reflected light must lie within the UN R48 limits for the night-time colour (red for a rear reflector).
Approval tests on the Class IA/IB retro-reflector samples must follow the chronological order in Table 4, starting with a visual inspection of general specifications.

Retro-reflector samples must undergo the tests in the Table 4 order, including the heat test (48 h at 65° ± 2°C) with visual inspection, colorimetry and photometry, water, fuel, oil and corrosion tests as listed.
The communication form must state the name and address of the manufacturer of the retro-reflective device.
If applicable, the form must state the name and address of the manufacturer's representative.
The form must state the date the device was submitted for approval tests and the technical service responsible for the approval test.
The form must state the date of the test report issued by the technical service.
The form must state the number of the test report issued by the technical service.

The form must give a concise description: whether the device is in isolation or part of an assembly, the colour of light emitted, whether it is installed as an integral part of a lamp integrated into the vehicle body, the geometric installation conditions, and whether it is for a limited mounting height of 750 mm or less.
The form must indicate the position of the approval mark or Unique Identifier (UI).
The form must state whether approval was granted, refused, extended or withdrawn.
If applicable, the form must state the reason(s) for the extension of approval.
The form must state the place of issue.
The form must state the date.

Production retro-reflective devices must conform mechanically and geometrically. Differences from the approved type may not exceed inevitable manufacturing deviations within the Regulation's requirements.
Photometric conformity of a randomly chosen retro-reflective device is not contested if no measured value is more than 20% below the minimum values prescribed in the Regulation.
The chromaticity coordinates must be complied with.

For each retro-reflective device type, the approval mark holder must carry out at least the specified tests at appropriate intervals. If sampling shows non-conformity, further samples must be taken and the manufacturer must act to ensure conformity.
The manufacturer's conformity tests must cover photometric and colorimetric characteristics and resistance to penetration of water.
Conformity tests must generally be carried out using the methods set out in the Regulation.
Equivalent test methods may be used in manufacturer conformity tests only with the Type Approval Authority's consent. The manufacturer must prove the methods are equivalent.
Where the manufacturer's own or equivalent test methods are used, test apparatus must be regularly calibrated and correlated with the Type Approval Authority's measurements.
The reference methods are always those of the Regulation, particularly for administrative verification and sampling.
Retro-reflective device samples must be selected at random from a uniform batch of the same type. The assessment generally covers series production from individual factories.
Sampled retro-reflective devices must be subjected to photometric measurements at the specified points and chromaticity coordinates.

The manufacturer must carry out a statistical study of test results and define acceptability criteria in agreement with the Type Approval Authority. The criteria must give a 95% minimum probability of passing a spot check at 95% confidence.
For a randomly chosen retro-reflective device, no measured photometric value may deviate unfavourably by more than 20% from the minimum values prescribed.
Chromaticity coordinates of the retro-reflective device must be complied with.

First sampling takes four randomly selected retro-reflective devices, split into samples A and B. Conformity is contested if any specimen deviates by more than 20%, and the manufacturer must then align production for repeated sampling.
After alignment, conformity is not contested if no specimen of samples C and D deviates by more than 20%.

If a specimen of samples C or D deviates by more than 20% but no specimen by more than 30%, the manufacturer must align production, and a second repeated sampling is carried out within two months of notification.
If a specimen of samples C and D deviates by more than 30%, the approval is withdrawn.
For samples E and F, conformity is not contested if no specimen deviates by more than 20%.
If a specimen of samples E or F deviates by more than 20%, conformity is contested and approval is withdrawn under paragraph 3.6.
One retro-reflector of sample A must pass the water-penetration test (Annex 6 Part 2, paragraph 1). If it fails, both devices of sample B must be tested and both must pass.
When measuring RI at β1 = β2 = 0°, check for mirror effect by slightly turning the device. If there is one, take a reading at β1 = -5°, β2 = 0°.

For retro-reflective devices not marked "TOP", measure RI at β1=β2=0° (or the specified angle) and 20' divergence. Rotate the device about its reference axis to the minimum-RI position, which must meet the specified value. The device may be rotated ±5° if the value is not attained.

For retro-reflective devices marked "TOP", rotate the device about its axis by ±5° at β1=β2=0° (or the specified angle) and 20' divergence. RI must not fall below the prescribed value in any position during the rotation.
If RI at β1=β2=0° and ε=0° exceeds the specified value by 50% or more, make all measurements for all illumination and divergence angles at ε=0°.
Use the CIE angular system (Figure A4-I) to specify and measure the retro-reflective device.
Illuminate retro-reflective devices with CIE Standard Illuminant A when testing retro-reflection. Measure as described in Part 1 of Annex 4.
Measuring geometry must satisfy source angular diameter δ≤10', measuring device angular diameter γ≤10' and illuminated area angular diameter η≤80'.
Avoid stray reflections during photometric measurements by appropriate masking (recommended).
For retro-reflector photometry, choose a measuring distance that respects at least the limits for angles δ, γ and η, and is not lower than 10 m.

Illuminance over the useful area of the retro-reflective device, measured perpendicular to the incident light, must be sufficiently uniform. It is checked with a measuring element no larger than one-tenth of the examined area, and max/min must be ≤ 1.05.
The photometer head must be corrected to the spectral luminous efficiency for the CIE standard photometric observer in photopic vision.
The photometer head must not show a perceptible change in local sensitivity within its aperture. Otherwise suitable provisions, such as a diffusing window, must be added.

Minimize stray light errors. Restrict as much as possible the field of view of the photometer head and the spread of light from the sample and the source. The background and sample holder framework should be matt black.
Reflections from the floor and walls over the long test distances must be screened from both the sample and the photometer head by baffles.
Measure residual stray light with the sample covered by an opaque matt black surface or equivalent, and subtract it from the value measured on the retro-reflective device.

The light source and photometer head should remain stable throughout the test. Laboratory ambient temperature should not vary significantly, and the apparatus should be allowed to stabilize before measurements.
The illuminating surface shape of the retro-reflector must not be easily confused with the triangular shape of Class IIIA/IIIB retro-reflectors when viewed from 10 m.
The moulded plastics retro-reflector (Class IA/IB) must be kept for 48 consecutive hours in a dry atmosphere at 65 °C ± 2 °C, then cooled for 1 hour at 23 °C ± 2 °C.
After the heat test, no cracking or appreciable distortion of the retro-reflective device, in particular its optical component, may be visible.

The retro-reflective device, stripped of removable parts, must be immersed for 10 minutes in water at 50 °C ± 5 °C with its upper illuminating surface 20 mm below the water surface. The test is repeated turned through 180°, then followed by immersion in water at 25 °C ± 5 °C.
No water shall penetrate to the reflecting surface of the retro-reflecting optical unit. Visible water means the device fails.

The retro-reflective device must be designed to retain the prescribed photometric and colorimetric characteristics despite the humidity and corrosive influences it is normally exposed to. Resistance to tarnishing of the front surface and to deterioration of the rear-face protection is checked, particularly where an essential metal component could be attacked. Corrosion testing follows ISO 9227:2017.

The retro-reflective device, or the lamp if combined with a light, must have all removable parts stripped. It must then be subjected to saline mist for 50 hours, as two 24-hour exposures separated by a 2-hour drying interval.
Immediately after the corrosion test, the sample must not show signs of excessive corrosion liable to impair the efficiency of the device.

After the corrosion test and a 48 h recovery (Annex 6 Part 2), with salt deposits cleaned off, RA of the retro-reflective areas at β2 = 5° and α = 20' must be not less than the Table 9 value and not more than the Table 10 value.
The weathering apparatus must comply with EN ISO 4892-1:2016 and EN ISO 4892-2:2013. It must control temperature and relative humidity and have a water spray system.
The water spray system must be capable of spraying at least 0.3 ml/cm² within 5 minutes.
The spray water must meet the requirements of EN ISO 4892-2:2013.
Test temperature must be measured with either a Black-Standard or a Black-Panel thermometer (test method TM1 or TM2).
The test method used (TM1 or TM2) must be specified in the report.
Samples must be exposed per EN ISO 4892-2:2013 using the Table A6-1 parameters. Retro-reflective devices are exposed for 500 hours.

Weathering exposure must use the Table A6-1 parameters: TM1 or TM2, with 102 min dry and 18 min water spray cycles, irradiance of 60±2 W/m² broadband and 0.51±0.02 W/m² at 340 nm, black-standard temperature 65±3 °C (TM1) or black-panel temperature 63±3 °C (TM2), and relative humidity 50±10 %.
Resistance to fuels must be tested with a mixture of 70 vol. % n-heptane and 30 vol. % toluol applied to the retro-reflective device.
The outer and illuminating surface of the retro-reflective device must be lightly wiped with a cotton cloth soaked in the test mixture.
After about five minutes the surface must show no apparent surface changes when inspected visually. Slight surface cracks are not objected to.
The outer (illuminating) surface of the retro-reflector is lightly wiped with a cotton cloth soaked in detergent lubricating oil. After about 5 minutes the surface is cleaned.
After the oil exposure and cleaning, the retro-reflective intensity (RI) is measured according to paragraph 5.1.3.2.2.

The application for approval must be submitted by the holder of the trade name or mark, or by a duly accredited representative. Any permitted installation inclinations or rotation about the reference axis must be indicated in the communication form if the applicant chooses to specify them.
For each type of reversing lamp, the application must be accompanied by the documents and samples listed in the following sub-clauses.

Submit drawings in triplicate, detailed enough to identify the lamp type. They must show the mounting position(s) on the vehicle, the axis of reference, the centre of reference, and the position intended for the approval mark. Mounting height and orientation are required only for manoeuvring lamps.

Submit a brief technical description. Unless the lamp has non-replaceable light sources, it must state the prescribed filament lamp category, LED light source category, or light source module identification code.
Submit two samples. Symmetrical left/right devices may be submitted as two identical samples for one side.
The lamp submitted for approval must bear the applicant's trade name or mark, clearly legible and indelible.
The lamp must provide adequate space for the approval mark and the additional symbols prescribed in paragraph 4.3, and the space must be shown in the drawing referred to in paragraph 2.2.1.

The approved reversing lamp must bear, in the space provided, an international approval mark consisting of a circle around the letter E followed by the approving country's number, and an approval number.
Reversing lamps must carry the additional symbol of letters A and R, arranged as shown in Annex 2.

Each lamp in a grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated assembly must satisfy the requirements of this Regulation or of another Regulation. A lamp that satisfies none of them must not be part of the assembly.

A single approval mark on the combined lamp consists of a circle around 'E', the country's distinguishing number, an approval number and, if necessary, the required arrow. It may be placed anywhere on the lamp, subject to the visibility and non-removability conditions.
The single approval mark must be visible after the lamp is installed.
No light-transmitting part of the combined lamp may be removable without also removing the approval mark.

Mark the identification symbol for each lamp under each Regulation approved, together with the corresponding amendment series incorporating the most recent major technical amendments at the time of issue of the approval.
For grouped/combined lamps, the identification symbol of each lamp must be marked either on the appropriate light-emitting surface of that lamp.
Alternatively, the marks may be placed on the group so that each grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamp can be clearly identified.
The components of a single approval mark must be no smaller than the minimum size required for the smallest individual mark under the Regulations by which approval was granted.
An approval number must be assigned to each approved type. The same Contracting Party may not give the same number to another type of grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps.
The approval mark and symbol must be indelible and clearly legible even when the reversing lamp is mounted on the vehicle.

The requirements of R48 (or R86) sections 5 and 6 and their referenced annexes apply. Requirements pertinent to the lamp and the vehicle category it is intended for must be applied where they can be verified at lamp type approval.
Each sample must conform to the specifications in the following paragraphs.
The reversing lamp must be designed and built so that it keeps working satisfactorily and retains its prescribed characteristics in normal use despite vibration.
The light intensity of each of the two samples must be within the specified minima and maxima, measured relative to the axis of reference in the directions specified.
The reversing lamp intensity along the axis of reference must be at least 80 cd.
Emitted intensity in any observable direction must not exceed 300 cd at or above the horizontal plane. Below the horizontal it must not exceed 600 cd between h-h and 5° D, or 8,000 cd below 5° D.

In every other direction of measurement in Annex 3, the luminous intensity must be not less than the minima in that annex. If the lamp is installed only as a pair, verification may stop at 30° inwards with at least 25 cd. That condition must be declared in the application and in the communication form comments.
The voltage to be applied to the lamp must be indicated in the communication form specified in Annex 1.

For non-filament lamps, the luminous intensities measured after 1 minute and after 10 minutes of operation must meet the minimum and maximum requirements. They are evaluated against the distribution at photometric stability, defined as less than 3% variation within any 15-minute period.
Determine the limits of the apparent surface of the light-signalling device (reversing lamp) in the direction of the reference axis.

The colour of the light emitted by the reversing lamp inside the light distribution grid field must be white, with no sharp colour variation outside this field. Colorimetry is checked with the test procedure of paragraph 7. For lamps with non-replaceable light sources, it is verified with the light sources present in the lamp.
Conformity of production procedures must comply with those in the Agreement, Appendix 2, together with the R23 requirements that follow.
Lamps must be manufactured to conform to the approved type. Compliance with the requirements of paragraphs 6 and 8 must be verified.
The minimum conformity of production control requirements in Annex 4 must be complied with.
The minimum requirements for sampling by an inspector in Annex 5 must be complied with.
The approval authority may verify conformity control methods in each production facility at any time. The normal frequency is once every two years.
Production reversing lamps bearing the approval mark must conform to the approved type. Otherwise the approval may be withdrawn.
If the approval holder completely ceases to manufacture an approved type of reversing lamp, it must inform the authority that granted the approval.

The approval communication must include a concise description of the lamp. This covers the number, category and kind of light source(s), voltage and wattage, control gear and light source module details, installation geometry, and maximum mounting height where applicable.
The communication must state the position of the approval mark on the lamp.
For a reversing lamp, the communication must state whether the device shall be installed on a vehicle only as part of a pair of devices (yes/no).

Where two or more lamps are part of the same assembly of grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps, the device is marked with a single approval mark (models B, C or D). The reversing lamp function is identified by AR.
Stray reflections must be avoided by appropriate masking during photometric measurements.
If results are challenged, the measurement distance must be such that the inverse square law applies.
If results are challenged, the angle subtended by the receiver from the reference centre of the light must be between 10' and 1°.
If results are challenged, the intensity requirement for a direction is met if the required intensity is obtained in a direction deviating by no more than a quarter of a degree.

For reversing lamp photometry, H=0° and V=0° correspond to the axis of reference. On the vehicle this axis is horizontal, parallel to the median longitudinal plane and oriented in the required direction of visibility. It passes through the centre of reference. The table gives the minimum intensities in cd for each direction.

If visual examination reveals substantial local variations of intensity, check that no intensity measured between two prescribed measurement directions is below 50 per cent of the lower of the two prescribed minimum intensities.
Conformity from a mechanical and geometric standpoint is satisfied if differences do not exceed inevitable manufacturing deviations within the requirements of the Regulation.

Conformity of mass-produced lamps is not contested if, in photometric testing of a randomly chosen lamp per paragraph 7, no measured value deviates unfavourably by more than 20 per cent from the prescribed values.
Chromaticity coordinates shall be complied with when tested under the conditions of paragraph 7 of the Regulation.

The approval mark holder must carry out at least the Annex 4 tests for each lamp type, at appropriate intervals. If sampling shows non-conformity, further samples must be taken and the manufacturer must act to restore conformity of production.
Conformity tests must cover photometric and colorimetric characteristics.
Conformity tests must generally be carried out in accordance with the methods set out in UN R23.
Equivalent test methods may be used only with the competent authority's consent. The manufacturer must prove the methods are equivalent to those in UN R23.
Test apparatus must be regularly calibrated and its measurements correlated with those of a competent authority.
The reference methods are those of UN R23, in particular for administrative verification and sampling.

Lamp samples must be selected at random from a uniform batch of the same type. The assessment generally covers series production of individual factories, and records from several factories may be grouped only if they operate under the same quality system and management.
The sampled lamp must be photometrically measured for the minimum values at the Annex 3 points and for the required chromaticity coordinates.

The manufacturer must carry out a statistical study of the test results and define acceptability criteria in agreement with the competent authority. With a 95% confidence level, the minimum probability of passing an Annex 5 first-sampling spot check must be 0.95.
Mass-produced lamps are considered conforming mechanically and geometrically if differences from the requirements do not exceed inevitable manufacturing deviations.
Photometric conformity of mass-produced lamps is not contested if a randomly chosen lamp, tested per paragraph 7, meets the paragraph 6 photometric performance (criteria in sub-paragraphs).
The requirements in paragraph 1.2.1 of Annex 4 must be met for photometric conformity of production.
Lamps with apparent defects are disregarded in the photometric conformity sampling.
Chromaticity coordinates shall comply when tested under paragraph 7 of the Regulation.
First sampling: four lamps selected at random, two marked A and two marked B.

Conformity is not contested if the deviation of every specimen of samples A and B is not more than 20 per cent. Measurement can be closed if both lamps of sample A deviate by not more than 0 per cent.

Conformity is contested if at least one specimen of A or B deviates by more than 20 per cent. The manufacturer must align production and repeated sampling is carried out within two months of notification. Samples A and B are retained by the Technical Service until conformity of production is finished.
First repeated sampling: four lamps selected at random from stock manufactured after alignment, two marked C and two marked D.

In first repeated sampling, conformity of mass-produced reversing lamps is not contested if the deviation of every specimen of samples C and D (four lamps) is at most 20 per cent. The measurement can be closed if both lamps of sample C deviate by 0 per cent.

If one specimen of samples C or D deviates by more than 20 per cent but no specimen deviates by more than 30 per cent, conformity is contested. The manufacturer must align production, and a second repeated sampling must be carried out within two months of notification. Samples C and D are retained by the Technical Service until the CoP process ends.
If one specimen of samples C and D deviates by more than 30 per cent, the approval is withdrawn and paragraph 5 of Annex 5 applies.
For the second repeated sampling, select four lamps at random from stock manufactured after alignment. Mark the first two as sample E and the second two as sample F.

In second repeated sampling, conformity is not contested if every specimen of samples E and F (four lamps) deviates by at most 20 per cent. The measurement can be closed if both lamps of sample E deviate by 0 per cent.
If at least one specimen of samples E or F deviates by more than 20 per cent, conformity is contested, the approval is withdrawn, and paragraph 5 of Annex 5 applies.
Approval withdrawal following failed CoP sampling must be carried out according to paragraph 10 of R23.
The application for approval must be submitted by the holder of the trade name or mark, or by an accredited representative.

The application must include drawings in triplicate, in sufficient detail to identify the type. They must show the fitting positions on the vehicle and the position intended for the approval number and class indicator relative to the approval mark circle. For Class IB or IIIB, installation details are also required.
The application must include a brief description giving the technical specifications of the materials of the retro-reflecting optical unit.
Every retro-reflecting device submitted for approval must bear the trade name or mark of the applicant.
A space of sufficient size for the approval mark must be provided on every device and shown on the drawings.
Markings must be visible from the outside when the retro-reflecting device is fitted on the vehicle.
Markings on the retro-reflecting device must be clearly legible and indelible.
An approval number is assigned to each approved type; its first two digits show the series of amendments, and the same number is not assigned to another type except for a colour-only extension.

Affix to the retro-reflecting device, in the space under 4.2 and in addition to the 4.1 markings, an international approval mark made up of a circle around 'E' and the country number, an approval number, and the class symbol (IA, IB, IIIA, IIIB or IVA).

In a unit of grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps including a retro-reflector, approval is granted only if each lamp satisfies R3 or another applicable Regulation. A lamp that does not satisfy one of those Regulations cannot be part of the unit.

If the combined lamps comply with several Regulations, a single approval mark (circle with E, country number, approval number and arrow if necessary) may be applied anywhere on the unit, provided the mark is visible after installation and cannot be separated from the light-transmitting parts.
The single approval mark on the combined lamp must be visible after installation.
No light-transmitting part of the combined lamps can be removed without also removing the approval mark.

Mark the identification symbol for each lamp, appropriate to each Regulation under which approval was granted, together with the series of amendments incorporating the most recent major technical amendments at the time of issue of the approval.

The identification symbol of each lamp in the grouped/combined unit must be marked on the appropriate light-emitting surface. This is one of two alternatives, the other being group marking under 5.6.2.2.
Alternatively, the identification symbols may be marked as a group so that each grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamp can be clearly identified.
The components of a single approval mark must not be smaller than the minimum size required for the smallest of the individual marks under the Regulations by which approval was granted.
An approval number is assigned to each approved type, and the same Contracting Party may not assign the same number to another type of grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps.
The approval mark must be clearly legible and indelible.

The pertinent requirements of the sections on general and individual specifications and the Annexes referenced in them (Regulation 48 and others, series of amendments in force at the time of application) apply to the retro-reflecting device for its vehicle category, where verification at type approval is feasible.
Retro-reflecting devices must function satisfactorily in normal use and must not have design or manufacturing defects that harm efficient operation or maintenance in good condition.
The components of the retro-reflecting device must not be capable of being easily dismantled.
Retro-reflecting optical units may not be replaceable.
The outer surface of the retro-reflecting device must be easy to clean: it must not be rough, and any protuberances must not prevent easy cleaning.
There must be no access to the inner surface of the retro-reflectors when in normal use.

The retro-reflecting device must satisfy the dimension and shape, colorimetric, photometric, physical and mechanical requirements of Annexes 5 to 11 and 13. Test procedures are in Annex 4 (Class IA, IIIA), Annex 14 (Class IVA) and Annex 16 (Class IB, IIIB).
Retro-reflectors must be manufactured to conform to the type approved under this Regulation, with compliance with paragraphs 6 and 7 verified.
Conformity of production control procedures must comply with the minimum requirements of Annex 17.
Sampling by an inspector must comply with the minimum requirements of Annex 18.
A retro-reflecting device bearing the approval mark must conform to the approved type and comply with the requirements, or its approval may be withdrawn.

The approval communication for the retro-reflecting device must give a concise description: whether it is in isolation or part of an assembly of devices, the colour of light emitted, whether it is integrated into a lamp that is integrated into the vehicle body, the geometric installation conditions, and whether it is for limited mounting height (750 mm or less).
The communication must state the position of the approval mark on the retro-reflecting device.

Where the retro-reflector is part of a unit of grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps, the unit's approval marking may follow the simplified marking models (D, E, F). The mark must identify each function and its Regulation and series of amendments.
The shape of the illuminating surface of the Class IA or IB retro-reflector must not be easily confused with a triangle at normal observation distances.
Compliance of the retro-reflector with the Annex 5 shape and dimension specifications must be verified by visual inspection.
If the retro-reflecting device is a combined retro-reflecting optical unit and filter, it must be designed so the parts cannot be separated under normal conditions of use.
Retro-reflecting optical units and filters must not be coloured by paint or varnish.

When illuminated by CIE standard illuminant A with 1/3 degree divergence at V=H=0 degrees (or V=±5 degrees, H=0 if the surface reflection is colourless), the trichromatic coordinates of the reflected light must be within the limits of paragraph 2.30 of Regulation No. 48.

The applicant must specify one or more axes of reference (or a range) corresponding to V=H=0 degrees. If more than one is specified, the photometric measurements must be repeated for each axis, or for the extreme axes of a range.

For photometric measurement, only the illuminating surface specified by the manufacturer is considered. For Class IA or IB it must lie within a 200 mm diameter circle and be limited to 100 cm². The manufacturer must specify the perimeter of the area used.

The CIL values of a red retro-reflector must be at least those in the table (Class IA/IB: 300/200/100 mcd/lx at 20' and 5/2.8/2.5 at 1°30', at the listed illumination angles). Lower values are not permitted within the stated solid angle.
When measuring CIL at V=H=0°, check whether a mirror effect occurs by slightly turning the device. If it does, take a reading at V=±5°, H=0° and adopt the position giving the minimum CIL.

For retro-reflecting devices not marked "TOP", at V=H=0° (or the paragraph 4 angle) and 20' divergence, rotate the device about its reference axis to the minimum-CIL position. That minimum must meet the paragraph 3 value. For the other angles, use the position corresponding to that value of ε, with ±5° rotation permitted if values are not met.
If CIL at V=H=0° and ε=0° exceeds the specified value by 50 % or more, make all measurements for all illumination and divergence angles at ε=0°.

Retro-reflecting devices, whether part of a lamp or not, must be stripped of removable parts and immersed for 10 minutes in water at 50±5 °C with the highest point of the illuminating surface 20 mm below the surface. Repeat after turning the device 180°, then immediately immerse in water at 25±5 °C under the same conditions.
After the submersion test, no water may reach the reflecting surface of the retro-reflecting optical unit. If visual inspection clearly shows water, the device fails.

If visual inspection shows no water or is in doubt, measure the CIL by the Annex 4 paragraph 3.2 or Annex 14 paragraph 4.2 method. First shake the retro-reflecting device lightly to remove excess water from the outside.

Retro-reflecting devices must keep their prescribed photometric and colorimetric characteristics despite humidity and corrosive influences. Resistance of the front surface to tarnishing and of the rear-face protection to deterioration must be checked, particularly where an essential metal component could be attacked.

The retro-reflecting device, or the lamp if the device is combined with a light, must be stripped of all removable parts and exposed to saline mist for 50 hours. This is two 24-hour exposures separated by a 2-hour drying interval.
The saline mist must be produced by atomizing, at 35 °C ± 2 °C, a solution of 20 ± 2 parts by weight of sodium chloride in 80 parts of distilled water with no more than 0.02% impurities.
Immediately after the salt-mist test, the sample must not show signs of excessive corrosion liable to impair the efficiency of the device.

The outer and illuminating surface of the retro-reflecting device is wiped with a cloth soaked in 70 vol.% n-heptane and 30 vol.% toluol. After about 5 minutes it must show no apparent surface changes; slight surface cracks are acceptable.

The outer and illuminating surface of the retro-reflecting device is wiped with a cloth soaked in detergent lubricating oil. After about 5 minutes it is cleaned, and the CIL is then measured per Annex 4 para 3.2 or Annex 14 para 4.2.
The retro-reflecting device must be kept for 48 consecutive hours in a dry atmosphere at 65 ±2 °C for the heat-resistance test.
After the heat test, no cracking or appreciable distortion of the retro-reflecting device, and in particular of its optical component, may be visible.
Production retro-reflectors must conform mechanically and geometrically, with differences not exceeding inevitable manufacturing deviations within the Regulation's requirements.
In mass production, no measured photometric value of a randomly chosen retro-reflector may deviate unfavourably by more than 20% from the prescribed minimum values.
Chromaticity coordinates of production retro-reflectors must be complied with.

For each retro-reflector type, the approval mark holder must carry out at least the specified conformity tests at appropriate intervals. If a sample is non-conforming, further samples are taken and the manufacturer must ensure production conformity.
Manufacturer conformity tests must cover the photometric and colorimetric characteristics and the resistance to penetration of water.
Conformity tests must generally follow the methods set out in the Regulation.
If the manufacturer uses equivalent test methods in conformity tests, it needs the competent authority's consent and must prove they are equivalent to the Regulation's methods.
The reference test methods for conformity verification and sampling are those of UN R3.
Retro-reflector samples for conformity checks must be selected at random from a uniform production batch of the same type.
Sampled retro-reflectors must undergo photometric measurements at the points, and chromaticity coordinates, specified in the Regulation.
The manufacturer must carry out a statistical study of test results and define acceptability criteria in agreement with the competent authority.
The acceptability criteria must give, at a 95 per cent confidence level, a minimum probability of 0.95 of passing an Annex 18 spot check (first sampling).
Photometric conformity is not contested if no measured value deviates unfavourably by more than 20 per cent from the minimum values prescribed in the Regulation.
Chromaticity coordinates must be complied with.

First sampling takes four randomly selected retro-reflectors, in samples A and B of two each. Conformity is contested if any specimen deviates by more than 20 per cent, and the manufacturer must then align production.
After the first repeated sampling, conformity is not contested if no specimen of samples C and D deviates by more than 20 per cent.

If one specimen of samples C or D deviates by more than 20 per cent but all deviate by no more than 30 per cent, the manufacturer must again align production. A second repeated sampling follows within two months of notification.

If a specimen of samples C or D deviates by more than 30 per cent, approval is withdrawn. The second repeated sampling (samples E and F) must have no deviation above 20 per cent, otherwise approval is withdrawn under paragraph 9.
One retro-reflector of sample A must pass the water-penetration test of Annex 8 para 1 (or Annex 14 para 3 for class IVA). If it fails, both retro-reflectors of sample B must pass.

The vehicle approval application must include a list of the prescribed lighting and light-signalling devices. Each device type, including this rear lamp, must be identified (component, type-approval mark, manufacturer, etc.).
If necessary to verify conformity, provide a layout drawing for each individual lamp showing the illuminating surface, light-emitting surface, axis of reference and centre of reference.
State the method used to define the apparent surface, declared for each lamp and recorded in item 10.2 of Annex 1.

For M and N category vehicles, provide a description of the electric power supply conditions for the listed devices (including the stop lamp), including any special power supply/electronic light source control gear or variable intensity control, if applicable.

Lighting and light-signalling devices must be fitted so that, under normal conditions of use and despite vibration, they retain the prescribed characteristics and let the vehicle comply with the Regulation. It must not be possible for the lamps to be inadvertently maladjusted.

Fitted reference axis must be parallel to the vehicle's road bearing plane. For rear signalling devices it must also be parallel to the median longitudinal plane. Tolerance is ±3° in each direction, and manufacturer fitting instructions must be complied with.
A tolerance of ±3° is allowed in each direction for the reference axis orientation.

Absent specific instructions, verify lamp height and orientation with the vehicle unladen on a flat, horizontal surface in the condition defined in 2.3.10, 2.3.10.1 and 2.3.10.2. If an AFS is installed, it must be in its neutral state.
Absent specific instructions, lamps forming a pair must be fitted symmetrically about the median longitudinal plane, judged by the lamp's exterior geometrical form.
Paired lamps must be symmetrical to one another about the median longitudinal plane. This does not apply to the lamp's interior structure.
Lamps constituting a pair must satisfy the same colorimetric requirements.
Lamps constituting a pair must have substantially identical photometric characteristics. This does not apply to a matched pair of a function and/or an AFS.
Lamps may be grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated only if all requirements on colour, position, orientation, geometric visibility, electrical connections and any others are fulfilled.

Each lamp's photometric and colorimetric requirements must be fulfilled with all other grouped, combined or incorporated functions switched OFF. When a rear position lamp is reciprocally incorporated with other functions that can be ON together with it, those functions' colour requirements must be fulfilled with both ON.
Measure maximum height above the ground from the highest point, and minimum height from the lowest point, of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis.
When reducing geometric visibility angles, measure the lamp's height above the ground from the H plane.

Position as regards width is taken from the edge of the apparent surface furthest from the median longitudinal plane (overall width), or from the inner edges (distance between lamps). Exact edges need not be determined where the position clearly meets the requirements.
In the absence of specific instructions, the photometric characteristics (intensity, colour, apparent surface, etc.) of the lamp must not be intentionally varied while it is switched ON.
Permitted variations in photometric characteristics (ambient light, other lamps ON/OFF, use for another function) must comply with the technical provisions for the lamp concerned.
Red light emitted by a lamp fitted on the rear of the vehicle must not be visible from the front of the vehicle.
Red lamps, except a red rearmost side-marker lamp, must not be directly visible towards the front. The check uses an observer moving within Zone 1 in a transverse plane 25 m in front of the vehicle.

In case of doubt about direct visibility, red light emitted to the front, as verified at lamp type approval, must be not more than 0.25 cd per lamp. The influence of the vehicle body is taken into account if applicable.

The vehicle's electrical connections must allow the rear position lamps, together with the other listed lamps (front position, end-outline marker, side-marker and rear registration plate lamps, where fitted), to be switched ON and OFF only simultaneously.
Lamps other than main-beam, dipped-beam and front fog headlamps must not be concealable. The rear position, stop and reversing lamps must remain non-concealed.
Light colours must follow the table: reversing lamp white, stop lamp red, rear position lamp red, rear retro-reflector red.
The number of lamps mounted on the vehicle must equal the number indicated in the individual specifications of the Regulation.

With the exception of retro-reflectors, the lamp must be able to operate by the sole installation of a light source and/or a fuse. Otherwise it is deemed not present, even if it bears an approval mark.

For M and N category vehicles, the applicant shall demonstrate to the Technical Service that the electric power supply conditions for the stop lamp and rear position lamp comply with the following provisions, with the vehicle electrical system at a constant voltage operating condition representative for the vehicle category.
Where 5.27.1 does not apply, the voltage at the terminals of the device(s) or function(s) shall not exceed 6.75 V (6 V systems), 13.5 V (12 V systems) or 28 V (24 V systems) by more than 3 per cent.
A report shall be attached to the approval documentation describing the methods used to demonstrate compliance with the electric power supply provisions and the results obtained.

No obstacle may lie inside the angles of geometric visibility to the propagation of light from any part of the lamp's apparent surface seen from infinity. Obstacles already present at the lamp's type-approval are disregarded.
If geometric visibility measurements are taken closer to the lamp, the direction of observation must be shifted parallel so the same accuracy is achieved.

If any part of the lamp's apparent surface is hidden by other vehicle parts when installed, proof must be furnished that the unhidden part still meets the photometric values prescribed for the device's approval.
An LED module need not be replaceable only if this is stated in the communication sheet of the component type approval.
Each lamp (device), where applicable, must be type approved under the corresponding device Regulation when installed on a vehicle.
A reversing lamp must be present. It is mandatory on motor vehicles and on trailers of categories O2, O3 and O4, and optional on O1 trailers.
On M1 vehicles (and other vehicles up to 6,000 mm long), fit one reversing lamp device. A second device is optional.
Reversing lamp devices must be type-approved to UN R23 (00 or later series) or UN R148 (00 or later series).
Mount the reversing lamp at least 250 mm and at most 1,200 mm above the ground.
Install the reversing lamp at the rear of the vehicle.
Vertical geometric visibility of the rear reversing lamp: 15° upwards and 5° downwards.
Horizontal geometric visibility: 45° to the right and left if there is only one device. If there are two devices, 45° outwards and 30° inwards.
The reversing lamp must be oriented rearwards.

The reversing lamp can be switched ON only if reverse gear is engaged and the propulsion start/stop control is in a position where the propulsion system can operate. It must not switch ON or stay ON if either condition is not met.
Stop lamps of category S1 or S2 are mandatory on all vehicle categories. S3 or S4 devices are mandatory on M1 and N1 vehicles, except chassis-cabs and N1 vehicles with open cargo space.
Fit two S1 or S2 category stop lamp devices and one S3 or S4 category device on the vehicle.
The stop lamp devices must be type-approved to UN R7 02 or later series, or to UN R148 00 or later series.

For M1/N1 vehicles, the S1 or S2 stop lamp's apparent surface point farthest from the median longitudinal plane (in the direction of the reference axis) must be no more than 400 mm from the vehicle's extreme outer edge.

The S1 or S2 stop lamp must be mounted not less than 350 mm and not more than 1,500 mm above the ground. The limit is 2,100 mm only if the bodywork makes 1,500 mm impossible and the optional lamps are not installed.
The S1 or S2 stop lamp must be mounted at the rear of the vehicle.

The S1 or S2 stop lamp must have horizontal geometric visibility of 45° to the left and right of the vehicle's longitudinal axis. The inward angle may be reduced to 20° under the H plane if the lamp is mounted below 750 mm.

The S1 or S2 stop lamp must have vertical geometric visibility of 15° above and below the horizontal. The downward angle may be reduced to 5° if the lamp is mounted below 750 mm. The upward angle may be reduced to 5° for an optional lamp mounted above 2,100 mm.
The stop lamp must be oriented towards the rear of the vehicle.
All stop lamps must be switched ON simultaneously when the braking system provides the relevant signal defined in UN Regulations Nos. 13 and 13-H.
A rear position lamp (devices of category R, R1 or R2) is mandatory on the vehicle.
Two rear position lamps must be fitted. They must be type-approved to UN R7 (02 or subsequent series) or UN R148 (00 or subsequent series).

The farthest point of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis must be no more than 400 mm from the extreme outer edge of the vehicle. For M1, the distance between the inner edges has no special requirement.

The rear position lamp must be mounted not less than 350 mm and not more than 1,500 mm above the ground. The limit is 2,100 mm only if the bodywork shape makes 1,500 mm impossible and the optional lamps are not installed.
The rear position lamp must be located at the rear of the vehicle.
Rear position lamp must be visible within a horizontal angle of 45° inwards and 80° outwards. The inward angle may be reduced to 20° under the H plane if the lamp is mounted below 750 mm.

Rear position lamp must be visible within a vertical angle of 15° above and below the horizontal. The downward angle may be reduced to 5° if the lamp is mounted below 750 mm. The upward angle may be reduced to 5° for an optional lamp mounted above 2,100 mm.
Rear position lamp orientation must be rearwards.

Electrical connections of the rear position lamp must be in accordance with paragraph 5.11. The OFF-during-indicator exception applies only if the lamp is reciprocally incorporated with a direction-indicator.

A closed-circuit tell-tale is mandatory and must be combined with that of the front position lamps. It is not required when daytime running lamps are ON. A failure tell-tale is mandatory only if the component Regulation requires it.
A non-triangular rear retro-reflector must be present on motor vehicles (mandatory).

Fit two retro-reflectors type-approved as Class IA or IB under UN R3 (02 or later series) or UN R150 (00 or later series). Additional retro-reflecting devices are permitted if they do not impair the mandatory lighting and signalling devices.

The point of the retro-reflector's illuminating surface farthest from the median longitudinal plane must be no more than 400 mm from the extreme outer edge of the vehicle. For M1 there is no special requirement on the distance between inner edges.
Mount the retro-reflector 250 mm to 900 mm above the ground. The upper limit is 1,200 mm if grouped with rear lamp(s), or 1,500 mm if the bodywork shape makes the lower limits impossible.
The rear retro-reflector must be positioned at the rear of the vehicle (in length).

Geometric visibility of the retro-reflector: horizontal 30° inwards and outwards; vertical 10° above and below horizontal. The downward angle may be reduced to 5° where the retro-reflector is mounted below 750 mm.
The rear retro-reflector must be oriented rearwards.
The illuminating surface of the retro-reflector may have parts in common with the apparent surface of any other lamp at the rear. This is a permission, not a mandate.

When the vehicle's DRLs are ON, the rear position lamps must be switched ON. They may be switched OFF only while ambient light outside the vehicle is above 7,000 lux, measured per Annex 13. Other lamps listed in paragraph 5.11 may also be switched ON.

The emergency stop signal, mandatory on motor vehicles, shall be given by the simultaneous operation of all the stop or direction-indicator lamps fitted as described in paragraph 6.23.7. The rear lamp's stop lamp is among the lamps that operate.
The number of lamps giving the emergency stop signal must be as specified for stop lamps (6.5.2) or direction-indicator lamps (6.7.2).
The arrangement of the emergency stop signal lamps must be as specified for stop lamps (6.5.3) or direction-indicator lamps (6.7.3).
The position of the emergency stop signal lamps must be as specified for stop lamps (6.5.4) or direction-indicator lamps (6.7.4).
The geometric visibility of the emergency stop signal lamps must be as specified for stop lamps (6.5.5) or direction-indicator lamps (6.7.5).
The orientation of the emergency stop signal lamps must be as specified for stop lamps (6.5.6) or direction-indicator lamps (6.7.6).
All lamps of the emergency stop signal must flash in phase at a frequency of 4.0 ± 1.0 Hz.
The emergency stop signal must operate independently of other lamps.
The emergency stop signal must be switched ON and OFF automatically.
The emergency stop signal may be switched ON only when vehicle speed is above 50 km/h and the braking system provides the emergency braking logic signal defined in UN R13 and R13-H.
The emergency stop signal must switch OFF automatically if the emergency braking logic signal (UN R13/R13-H) is no longer provided or if the hazard warning signal is activated.
State in the R48 communication whether reversing lamps are fitted (yes/no, striking out what does not apply). For this product the answer is yes.
State in the R48 communication whether stop-lamps are fitted (yes/no, striking out what does not apply). For this product the answer is yes.
State in the R48 communication whether rear position lamps are fitted (yes/no, striking out what does not apply). For this product the answer is yes.
The vehicle approval communication must state, yes or no, whether rear non-triangular retro-reflectors are fitted. This is the device included in the rear lamp.

Check the position of lamps in width, height and length against the general requirements of paragraphs 2.10.2., 2.10.3., 2.10.4., 2.3.3. and 5.4. The measured distances must fulfil the individual specifications applicable to each lamp.

Check the angles of geometric visibility per paragraph 2.10.7. The measured angles must meet the individual specifications for each lamp. The limits may have an allowance corresponding to the ±3º mounting variation permitted in paragraph 5.3.

Check the visibility of red light towards the front and of white light towards the rear in accordance with paragraph 5.10 of UN R48. The red rear lamp functions must not be visible from the front, and white light must not be visible to the rear except as 5.10 allows for reversing lamps.

Check the electrical connections by switching on every lamp. The lamps and tell-tales must function in accordance with paragraphs 5.11 to 5.14 of UN R48 and the individual specifications for each lamp.
