The application for approval must be submitted by the holder of the trade name or mark, or by their duly accredited representative.
The application must specify the purpose or purposes for which the device is intended and whether it may also be used in an assembly of two lamps of the same kind or type.
The application must specify whether the device produces steady luminous intensity (R, R1, RM1, S1, S3) or variable luminous intensity (R2, RM2, S2, S4).

The application must include drawings, in triplicate, detailed enough to identify the device type. They must show the mounting position(s), the axis and centre of reference, the geometrical installation conditions meeting paragraph 6, any interdependent lamp combination, and the position of the approval mark.

Provide a brief technical description stating the prescribed LED light source category (UN R128) and/or the light source module identification code. The filament category (UN R37) applies only if filament sources are used. Lamps with non-replaceable light sources are excepted. The S3/S4 rear-window specification applies only to inside-mounted S3/S4 lamps.
Submit two samples. If the devices are not identical but are symmetrical for left and right mounting, the two samples may be identical and suitable for only one side.
The device must bear the applicant's trade name or mark, clearly legible and indelible.
The lamp must include a space of sufficient size for the approval marking and the additional symbols, shown in the drawings.
Each lamp in a grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated unit must satisfy this Regulation or another Regulation. A lamp that satisfies none of them shall not be part of the unit.

An approval number is assigned to each approved type. Its first two digits show the series of amendments. The same number shall not be assigned to another device type, except when approval is extended to a device that differs only in the colour of light emitted.
Every device conforming to an approved type must bear an approval mark, in the marking space and in addition to the other required markings.
The approval mark must include a circle surrounding the letter "E" followed by the distinguishing number of the country that granted approval.
The approval mark must include the approval number prescribed in paragraph 4.1.3.
The approval mark must include the additional symbol or symbols prescribed in the following sub-paragraphs for the lamp functions covered by UN R7.
Devices meeting UN R7 as rear position lamps must be marked with the letter "R". The letter is optionally followed by "1" for steady intensity or by "2" for variable intensity.
Devices meeting UN R7 as stop-lamps must be marked with the letter "S". The letter is followed by 1 (steady), 2 (variable), 3 (category S3, steady) or 4 (category S4, variable).
Devices comprising both a rear position lamp and a stop-lamp meeting UN R7 must be marked with the letters "R", "R1" or "R2" and "S1" or "S2" as applicable, separated by a horizontal dash.
Approval marks and symbols must be clearly legible and indelible, even when the device is fitted in the vehicle.

If the combined lamp is approved under several Regulations, a single international approval mark (circle with E, country number and approval number) may be used. It can be placed anywhere on the lamp only if the following conditions are met.
The single approval mark must be visible after the lamp is installed.
No light-transmitting part of the combined lamp may be removable without also removing the approval mark.
Mark the identification symbol for each lamp, appropriate to each Regulation under which approval is granted. Include the amendment series and the arrow if required.
Place the identification symbols either on the appropriate light-emitting surface of the lamp. The alternative is a group marking under 4.3.2.2.2.
Alternatively, mark the lamps as a group so that each grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamp can be clearly identified.
The components of a single approval mark must not be smaller than the minimum size required for the smallest of the individual marks under which approval is granted.
The approval marking must be clearly legible and indelible. It must be visible when the device is fitted on the vehicle or when a movable part such as the hood, boot lid or a door is opened.

Meet the requirements pertinent to each lamp and to the vehicle category it is installed on, taken from sections 5 and 6 and the referenced Annexes of UN R48 (or R53, R74, R86). These apply where verification at lamp type approval is feasible.
Each device supplied must conform to the specifications in paragraphs 6 and 8 of the Regulation.
The device must be designed and built so that, in normal use and despite vibration, it keeps working satisfactorily and keeps the characteristics prescribed by R7.

On the reference axis, the rear position lamp and stop lamp must emit at least the minimum and at most the maximum luminous intensity in the table. The table gives 4 to 17 cd for rear position lamps used as a single lamp.
A steady rear position lamp (category R or R1) must meet the intensity limits for that category.
The stop lamp must meet the minimum and maximum intensity for its category. Examples are S1 (steady) at 60 to 260 cd and S3 (steady) at 25 to 110 cd.
In a single lamp with more than one light source, a group of sources wired so that failure of any one makes all stop emitting light is considered one light source.

If any one light source fails in a single lamp with more than one light source, either the light intensity still meets the Annex 4 minimum, or a failure tell-tale signal is produced. The tell-tale option requires at least 50% of the minimum intensity on the reference axis and a note in the communication form.
In each direction in the Annex 4 light distribution table, intensity must be not less than the paragraph 6.1 minimum multiplied by the table percentage for that direction.
In no direction within the space from which the device is visible may intensity exceed the maximum in the paragraph 6.1 table.
Throughout the Annex 1 fields, luminous intensity must be not less than 0.05 cd for rear position lamps. The 0.3 cd and 0.07 cd values apply only to S-category stop lamp devices.
The Annex 4 paragraph 2.2 provisions on local variations of intensity must be observed.
Measure intensities with the light source(s) continuously alight, and for red-light devices in coloured light.
Use the measurement methods of Annex 4 (as referred to in paragraph 6.2.1) when measuring the lamp's light intensities.
Note the voltage to be applied to the lamp in the Annex 2 communication form.
Determine the limits of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis of the light-signalling device.

Light emitted inside the Annex 4 light distribution grid must be red or white, with no sharp colour variation outside it. Check it using the paragraph 7 test procedure. For lamps with non-replaceable light sources, verify with the light sources present in the lamp.
Conformity of production procedures must comply with those in the Agreement, Schedule 1.
Manufacture lamps to conform to the type approved under R7. Compliance with paragraphs 6 and 8 is verified.
Comply with the minimum conformity of production control requirements in Annex 5.
Comply with the minimum requirements for sampling by an inspector in Annex 6.
The manufacturer's production facility conformity control methods may be verified by the approving authority at any time, normally once every two years.
Approval may be withdrawn if the conformity conditions are not satisfied, so the lamp must continue to meet them.
If the approval holder completely ceases to manufacture a device approved under this Regulation, it must inform the authority that granted the approval.

The rear position lamp and stop lamp must meet minimum vertical light-distribution angles of 15° above and 15° below the horizontal. Exceptions: lamps with the H plane below 750 mm mounting height (15° above, 5° below), optional lamps above 2,100 mm (5° above, 15° below), and category S3/S4 stop lamps (10° above, 5° below). The horizontal angles follow the Annex 1 diagrams for rear position lamps and stop lamps.

The communication for the approved lamp type must describe it by lamp category. This covers colour of light emitted, number, category and kind of light source(s), voltage and wattage, mounting height, installation conditions, control gear or variable intensity, and any failure tell-tale condition.
The approval number and additional symbols must be placed close to the circle, either above or below the letter "E" or to its right or left.
Where two or more lamps are part of the same assembly (grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated), the approval marking may use the simplified marking arrangement shown in the models.
During photometric measurements, avoid stray reflections by appropriate masking.
When measurements are challenged, use a measurement distance at which the inverse-square law of distance applies.
When measurements are challenged, the receiver's angular aperture viewed from the lamp's reference centre shall be between 10 angular minutes and one degree.
Light distribution is measured relative to the reference axis (H=0°, V=0°), and the grid values give the minimum intensity in each direction as a percentage of the minimum required on the axis.
Within the grid field, the light pattern must be substantially uniform. In each direction, intensity must meet at least the lowest minimum percentage shown on the surrounding grid lines.
For a signalling lamp without filament light sources, luminous intensities measured after 1 minute and after 30 minutes of operation must comply with the minimum and maximum requirements.
Conformity of production is satisfied mechanically and geometrically if differences do not exceed inevitable manufacturing deviations within the requirements of the Regulation.
Mass-produced lamps must meet the photometric performances of paragraph 6 when tested per paragraph 7. Conformity is not contested if any randomly chosen lamp meets the criteria that follow.

No measured photometric value may deviate unfavourably by more than 20% from the prescribed values. For minimum values required throughout the Annex 1 fields, the maximum deviations follow the table (0.3 cd: 0.1 cd at 20%; 0.05 cd: 0.02 cd at 20%).
Colorimetric performance of production lamps must comply with paragraph 8 of UN R7.

For each lamp type, the approval holder must carry out at least the required tests at appropriate intervals, in accordance with the Regulation. If sampling shows non-conformity, further samples must be taken and tested, and the manufacturer must take steps to ensure production conformity.
Manufacturer conformity tests must cover the photometric and colorimetric characteristics.
CoP tests must generally be carried out in accordance with the methods set out in UN R7.
If equivalent test methods are used in manufacturer conformity tests, they require the competent authority's consent. The manufacturer must prove they are equivalent to the methods in the Regulation.
Where manufacturer test methods or equivalent methods are used, test apparatus must be regularly calibrated and correlated with measurements made by a competent authority.
The reference test methods are those of UN R7, particularly for administrative verification and sampling.

Lamps for conformity checks must be randomly sampled from a uniform batch of the same type. Assessment generally covers series production from individual factories. Records from several factories may be grouped only if they operate under the same quality system and management.
Sampled lamps must undergo photometric measurements for the minimum values at the Annex 4 points and for the required chromaticity coordinates.

The manufacturer must run a statistical study of test results and define, with the competent authority, acceptability criteria. The criteria must give, at 95% confidence, at least a 0.95 probability of passing an Annex 6 spot check (first sampling).
Mechanical and geometric conformity is satisfied if differences from the R7 requirements do not exceed inevitable manufacturing deviations.
Conformity of mass-produced lamps is not contested if a random lamp, tested per paragraph 7, meets the photometric performance of paragraph 6 under the conditions of the following sub-paragraphs.
Photometric conformity requires that the requirements in paragraph 1.2.1 of Annex 5 are met.
Lamps with apparent defects are disregarded in the conformity sampling.
In inspector sampling, the chromaticity coordinates of the lamps must comply when tested under the conditions of paragraph 7 of R7.
For the first sampling, four lamps are selected at random and split into sample A (two lamps) and sample B (two lamps).

Conformity of mass-produced lamps is not contested if no specimen of samples A and B (all four lamps) deviates by more than 20 per cent. Measurement can be closed if both lamps of sample A deviate by no more than 0 per cent.

If any specimen of sample A or B deviates by more than 20 per cent, conformity is contested. The manufacturer must bring production into line, and repeated sampling under para 3 must be done within two months of notification. Samples A and B are retained by the Technical Service until the conformity-of-production process is finished.
For the first repeated sampling, four lamps are selected at random from stock made after alignment and split into samples C and D (two lamps each).

Conformity is not contested if no specimen of samples C and D (all four lamps) deviates by more than 20 per cent. Measurement can be closed if both lamps of sample C deviate by no more than 0 per cent.

If one specimen of sample C or D deviates by more than 20 per cent, but all specimens deviate by no more than 30 per cent, the manufacturer must again bring production into line. A second repeated sampling under para 4 must follow within two months of notification. Samples C and D are retained by the Technical Service until the conformity-of-production process is finished.
If one specimen of sample C or D deviates by more than 30 per cent, the approval is withdrawn and para 5 of Annex 6 applies.
For the second repeated sampling, four lamps are selected at random from stock made after alignment and split into samples E and F (two lamps each).

Conformity is not contested if no specimen of samples E and F (all four lamps) deviates by more than 20 per cent. Measurement can be closed if both lamps of sample E deviate by no more than 0 per cent.
If at least one specimen of sample E or F deviates by more than 20 per cent, conformity is contested, the approval is withdrawn and para 5 of Annex 6 applies.
If conformity-of-production sampling shows the mass-produced lamps do not conform, the type approval for the rear position lamp and stop-lamp is withdrawn according to paragraph 10 of the Regulation.
